summary: Revise at 5.8 (Caiman 7, ship 7.5). The subject reads. At 300 px, uncaptioned, face-300 and hero-300 show a Gothic pointed arch: crockets climb the extrados to a fleur finial, a trefoil is pierced in the head, and capitals and abaci sit at the springers. That is a real win after the keel failed seven read tests. The workmanship is still a flat 2.5D cookie-cutter, though. Every element is a sketch extruded straight along the pull with square walls and no seam beads. The crockets are flat polygonal lobes, and their chords show in face.png and stones.png. The finial is a flat cross. The capitals and abaci are stacked boxes, and the palm is a square slab sill. This is exactly the 'stacked boxes' failure in house rule 10. Density is far below Caiman. The spandrel, the piers and the whole palm are bare flat metal, and the pier lancets are hairlines you cannot see at 300 px. Worn, the ring is seen from above (top.png): a plain band with a row of square teeth, which does not carry the theme the face view promises. The face is also 26.2 x 32.3 mm, with the apex 8.7 mm proud of the bore. The gates mostly verify, but the release study's status is 'Review' with 34 sand-slot findings, the field verdict is recorded as 'Castable with care', and the 0.075 run never reached its pitch. All three must be resolved or explicitly exempted in report.json before the ring can ship.
strengths: Immediate read at 300 px as a Gothic pointed arch: the equilateral head, crocketed extrados, finial and imposts are a clear cathedral vocabulary, and the silhouette is distinct from every other Tenebrae ring.
One theme face to palm: the whole ring is one arch on two piers, with nothing scattered.
Honest sand construction: every feature is drawn on the parting plane and extruded along the pull. Ray release is 0 obstructions and 0 unresolved at both pitches.
Clean geometry: watertight, single shell, 0 degenerate faces, 0 self-crossings, all 79 features Ok. The feature names are sentences, as house rule 9 asks.
The pierced trefoil in the head and the sunk order give the face a second plane of depth.

checklist.item: One theme face to palm, nothing scattered
checklist.reason: The whole ring is the arch: crockets and finial on the extrados, order and trefoil in the head, imposts at the springers, piers and sill at the palm. Nothing off-theme.

checklist.item: Reads as its Gothic subject at 300 px, not a perforated or grooved band
checklist.reason: face-300 and hero-300 read uncaptioned as a crocketed Gothic pointed arch with a finial. Caveat: the worn view (top.png, from above the hand) reads as a plain band with a row of square teeth, and the arch is visible only along the finger.

checklist.item: Figurative motifs have true outlines, crisp, no combing or stair-steps
checklist.reason: The outlines are true CAD silhouettes, but they are coarse polygons. In face.png the crocket lobes and the finial show visible chord facets of about 0.3-0.5 mm, and stones.png shows faceted crocket rims and flat-cut lobes. The crockets are blobs, not curled leaves; the brief's 'curled leaf hooking round the ring' is absent.

checklist.item: Stones in made settings, à jour, coloured as stained glass
checklist.reason: Not applicable: the brief carries no stones, and 0 are reported and 0 previewed.

checklist.item: No flat, blocky or mechanical CAD; forms sculpted
checklist.reason: Every part is a straight extrusion with square walls and no seam bead (house rule 10 requires blend_mm 0.1-0.35 on every join, and mouldings or chamfers on piers and plinths). In hero.png and shoulder.png the capitals and abaci are stacked boxes, the palm sill is a square slab with hard 90-degree corners (palm.png), and the crockets are flat plates standing on a flat extrados.

checklist.item: Factory stock keeps its hard wall-to-face angles
checklist.reason: Not applicable: this is a CAD-only ring with no factory stock.

checklist.item: Distinct silhouette; custom heads >= 13 mm; shoulder ornament not cut off
checklist.reason: The silhouette is unique in the collection. The face is 26.2 x 32.3 mm. The crocket run reaches the imposts and the order runs to the springers. Concern: at 32.3 mm tall with the apex 8.7 mm over the bore, it is a statement piece that will rock on the finger; see punch item 6.

checklist.item: Large, medium and small forms; density and legibility at least Caiman's
checklist.reason: The large form is strong, and the medium forms (crockets, imposts) are legible. There is almost no small form: the spandrel between keel and mouth is bare except one trefoil, the pier faces carry two hairline lancets that vanish at 300 px, the sill and palm are blank, and the extrados land is plain. It is far sparser than Caiman's hero or the Reptilia sheet.

punch_list.zone: Extrados, crockets (features 16-25, 'the crockets climbing the extrados to the finial') and the finial
punch_list.change: Replace the flat round lobes with true curled-leaf crockets. Each one is a stalk leaving the keel and a three-lobed leaf whose tip hooks back toward the apex, with an inner hook gap of at least 0.6 mm and strokes of at least 0.8 mm. Draw the outlines with no chord over 0.1 mm. Give each crocket a second, smaller tier (a leaf rib or curled tip 0.25 mm proud, drafted 3 degrees per half) so it has two planes. Redraw the finial as a fleuron with four crockets of its own: rounded, not a square-armed cross.
punch_list.acceptance: In face.png and stones.png no crocket or finial outline shows polygon facets. Each crocket reads as a hooked leaf at 300 px in face-300. The finial reads as a fleuron, not a plus sign.

punch_list.zone: Every join: keel flanks to land, crockets and finial to keel, capitals and abaci to piers (features 9, 15, 25, 47, 53)
punch_list.change: Add seam beads of blend_mm 0.2-0.3 on every joined part (house rule 10). Mould the imposts: a chamfered abacus (0.3 mm chamfer) over a capital with a cavetto or roll, not two stacked boxes. Round or chamfer every outer corner of 90 degrees or more by at least 0.3 mm.
punch_list.acceptance: hero.png, shoulder.png and side.png show no box-on-box imposts and no hard 90-degree concave seams. The capital reads as a moulded capital.

punch_list.zone: Palm and piers (sill y -11 to springers y -3; pier lancets features 54-59)
punch_list.change: The palm is a square slab. Give the sill a base moulding (plinth with a 0.4 mm chamfer and a roll), round its plan corners to at least 2 mm, and widen the pier lancets to 1.4 mm wide x 3.5 mm tall, sunk 0.6 mm. Use two per pier face, each with a cusped head, so the piers read as buttressed jambs.
punch_list.acceptance: The pier lancets are visible in face-300 at 300 px, and palm.png shows a moulded plinth rather than a flat rectangular slab.

punch_list.zone: Spandrel / tympanum between the order and the mouth (features 26-37, 60-69), both faces
punch_list.change: Fill the head with tracery. Enlarge the pierced trefoil to at least 2.8 mm and flank it with two mouchettes or two blind cusped lights in the spandrel's lower corners. Add a cusped (trefoil-foiled) inner edge to the order so the arch's intrados carries cusps. Keep bars at 0.8 mm or more and the lands asserted.
punch_list.acceptance: face-300 shows tracery across the head, not one small hole in flat metal. land_widths stay at or above 0.8 mm. Release stays at 0 obstructions.

punch_list.zone: Extrados land, the worn view (top.png), theta 0-360
punch_list.change: From above the hand the ring is a band with a row of square teeth. Turn the extrados land into a moulded keel: a central fillet and two hollow chamfers on the drafted flanks. Cut a row of small blind cusped niches (1.0 x 1.4 mm, 0.4 mm deep, cut along the pull) into each 37-degree flank between crockets, so the worn view carries the cathedral too.
punch_list.acceptance: In top.png the extrados reads as Gothic ornament (moulded keel with crocket heads and niches), not a toothed strip.

punch_list.zone: Overall proportion (arch radius 24.3, apex_y 18.04, bounds 26.2 x 32.3 mm)
punch_list.change: The apex stands 8.7 mm over the bore and the face is 32.3 mm tall. Lower the apex and finial by about 3 mm (target 29 mm or less overall) or confirm the scale with Logan. Either way, report the centre of mass offset from the bore, because a top-heavy arch will rotate on the finger.
punch_list.acceptance: report.json records the bounds and a centre-of-mass figure. Either the face is 29 mm or less tall, or Logan's sign-off on the scale is recorded.

punch_list.change: Resolve the release study's 'Review' status: locate the 34 sand-slot findings (0.07-0.60 mm, below the 0.6 mm sand web; likely the drafted-half overlap steps and the gaps between keel flank, order and crocket bases) and close or widen each to 0.6 mm or more. Re-run the 0.075 study at a true 0.075 pitch on both axes (raise the grid cap or tile it). Add explicit gate entries for the parts-only field exemption and for draft-clamp bites (not applicable).
punch_list.acceptance: release_0_100 and release_0_075 both report status other than 'Review' with 0 sand-slot findings below 0.6 mm, pitch at or below 0.075 on both axes, and the gates array names the field exemption explicitly. Template bytes stay under 300,000 after the additions.
